reason: Handing a jar to the user for a test in his own modpack is a recurring class of work (passes on NeoForge and Fabric, each with a numbered procedure and a log to read back). No existing skill covers the handoff: farfield-dev-client-check covers only the dev client run.

Step 3 forced a re-import for every pack test, but this episode's E.7 jar only changed rendering (texture colors, biome tints, water, fog); the agent told the user no re-import was needed and the skill was not updated, so the next session repeats the mismatch or contradicts the skill.
A mip-rule change makes the first open rebuild the coarse levels automatically; the pack-test procedure never mentioned it, so the user could judge the far view mid-rebuild or wrongly re-import.
The user reported already-known gaps as fresh observations at the previous pass; the procedure should list open gaps up front.

The user closed a visual pass with a verdict, and the closing commit ticked the plan item and logged the verdict. The skill says to log passes but not how a verdict closes a plan item or what scope exclusions to record, which the session had to improvise.
The fixed folder kept old -pre-alpha jars beside the new build, so the user could load the wrong file; the skill only says to overwrite the same version name.
A settings-screen pass is a new class of change: it touches no LOD data, so the procedure must skip the import and instead verify the saved values after a restart.

The user's pack log gave the proof for the dimension-change check (Nether to Overworld, then disconnect), but the skill names only the render and import lines and not where the pack's log lives or the client-mode lines.

The user deferred the pack test to the next session ("Je testerais la prochaine fois, on s'arrête là"). The closing message had to carry the whole resume procedure itself, so the skill should require that restated resume line whenever a test is deferred.
